TorrentPlayer 

 
 Stream at the speed of the swarm. 
 Movies, shows, music, podcasts, audiobooks: any torrent starts in seconds and skips to any
 moment in under a second, straight from the swarm. No servers, no accounts, no limits.

---

TorrentPlayer is a free, open-source desktop app that plays any torrent straight from
BitTorrent , video or audio, the way a streaming service would. Press play and it starts in
seconds; drag the seek bar to minute 47 and it is playing minute 47 a moment later, long before
the download gets there. No separate torrent client, no waiting for the file, no server in
between.

Use it for whatever you stream from torrents: films and series, music albums, podcasts,
audiobooks, lectures, and open media. You are responsible for having the right to download and
share what you play.

 Why TorrentPlayer

- Stream it. Skip it. Instantly. Most torrent players download from the start and make you
 wait for the part you want. TorrentPlayer's own streaming engine fetches the exact moment you
 jump to, first , so skipping ahead resumes in under a second: 0.3 s on a fast link and 0.7 s
 (median) on a public swarm in our measurements. Skip the intro, jump to the
 lecture's second half, scrub back and forth; it keeps up.
- Full speed, limited only by the swarm. Video comes directly from the people sharing it.
 How fast it arrives depends on the torrent's seeders and peers and on your own connection,
 never on a provider's plan, a server's capacity, or a "free tier".
- No servers, no dependencies. There is no TorrentPlayer streaming server, cloud cache, or
 relay, and no account to sign in to. Your computer talks to the swarm directly, so nothing
 in between can throttle it, fill up, or shut it off. (The built-in search asks a public
 torrent index; it is optional, and pasting a magnet link or opening a .torrent file needs
 nothing but the swarm.)
- None of the usual limits. No subscription, ads, watch-time limits, quality caps, storage
 quotas, or speed tiers. Watch at the quality the file has, for as long as you like.
- Private by design. No telemetry, analytics, or crash reporting. Built-in WireGuard and SOCKS5,
 with a kill switch that never falls back to a direct connection, or your own VPN app.
- Free and open source, every part of it, including the streaming engine. MIT or
 Apache-2.0, your choice.

 How it compares

 TorrentPlayer Stremio (torrent add-ons) WebTorrent Desktop qBittorrent + VLC Debrid / cloud services webtor.io (browser) 
 -------------------------------------- ----------------------------------- ---------------------------------------- -------------------- ----------------------------------- --------------------------------- ----------------------------- 
 Stream and skip anywhere ✅ the spot you skip to comes first ✅ ✅ ❌ plays in order only Only after the service fetches it ✅ via its servers 
 Video straight from peers, no server ✅ Via a local streaming server ✅ ✅ ❌ provider's servers ❌ webtor.io's servers 
 Speed limited only by the swarm ✅ ✅ ✅ ✅ ❌ plan and provider limits ❌ free speed cap, paid tiers 
 Free, no account ✅ ✅ free tier, guest mode ✅ ✅ ❌ paid plans ✅ basic use 
 Fully open source ✅ Partly (streaming server is proprietary) ✅ ✅ ❌ ✅ 
 Built-in VPN (WireGuard) + kill switch ✅ ❌ bring your own ❌ ❌ proxy and interface binding only Not applicable Not applicable 
 Queue that downloads ahead ✅ shares bandwidth with playback Paid plan ❌ As a download client Cloud storage Paid tiers 
 No telemetry ✅ ❌ analytics (per privacy policy) ❌ basic usage stats ✅ none documented Not checked Not checked 
 Actively maintained ✅ ✅ Last release 2020 ✅ ✅ ✅ 

Checked on 20 October 2026. Stremio and Kodi reach more devices (TVs, phones), and VLC- or
mpv-based players play more codecs today; see the full comparison for
sources, details, and where other tools are the better fit.

 Features

 Streaming built for skipping

- TorrentPlayer's own engine ( torrentplayer-swarm ), written for playback rather than bulk
 downloading. It requests the playhead first, then the file's index and a read-ahead window
 sized from the video's bitrate. When you skip, it cancels requests that are no longer
 urgent, sends the pieces at the new position to the fastest peers, and duplicates the most
 urgent blocks to a second peer so one slow peer cannot stall playback.
- Finds peers fast. HTTP and UDP trackers, the DHT, and peer exchange, with quick first
 connection attempts and peers that worked before tried first.
- Paste, drop, or search. Magnet links, .torrent files and links (drag one onto the
 window), or the built-in search.
- Instant start for the best result. Each search marks a "Best pick" and quietly preloads
 its first minutes, so pressing play on it starts at once. One preload at a time, never
 uploaded, deleted if unused, and off with one switch.

 A queue that downloads ahead, intelligently

- Everything you queue downloads in the background while you watch, so the next video is
 ready before you get to it. Set a maximum in Settings if you prefer fewer at once.
- What you are watching always comes first. Every second TorrentPlayer measures your
 connection and playback's needs. While the buffer is short, the rest of the queue gets only
 what playback leaves; if playback runs low, the rest pauses briefly to let it catch up, and
 keeps going if the video's own swarm is the bottleneck. Once you are comfortably ahead,
 everything runs at full speed again.
- Live status for every item: download and upload speed, peers, percent downloaded, and
 time left. Green sections show the downloaded chunk

install.title: Installing on Linux
install.html:
On Linux, WebKit plays audio and video through GStreamer, which needs several plugin packages. You don't install them yourself (since 0.3.3):

Package For GStreamer's plugins
AppImage Any distribution, including Arch and Manjaro Bundled inside the AppImage
.deb Debian, Ubuntu, Linux Mint, Pop!_OS Installed with TorrentPlayer by apt (declared dependencies)
.rpm Fedora, RHEL and its rebuilds, openSUSE Installed with TorrentPlayer by dnf or zypper

Install the .deb or .rpm with your package manager so it brings them along:

sudo apt install ./TorrentPlayer_<version>_amd64.deb         # Debian, Ubuntu, Mint, Pop!_OS
sudo dnf install ./TorrentPlayer-<version>-1.x86_64.rpm       # Fedora, RHEL, Rocky, Alma
sudo zypper install ./TorrentPlayer-<version>-1.x86_64.rpm    # openSUSE

Double-clicking the file in your software center works too. A bare dpkg -i or rpm -i does not install dependencies; if you used one, run sudo apt -f install (or install the file again with dnf or zypper). The video decoders (libav, and openh264 on Fedora and openSUSE, whose libav leaves H.264 out) are recommended packages, which package managers install by default; on Fedora openh264 comes from Cisco's repository, which Fedora enables by default. Upgrading to a new version installs any new dependencies the same way, and a new AppImage brings its own plugins. Every release installs each package on Ubuntu, Debian, Fedora, and openSUSE, and checks the AppImage on Arch, before it ships. If audio or video still plays silently or not at all, see Troubleshooting.

features.title: Features
features.html:
Streaming built for skipping
  • TorrentPlayer's own engine (torrentplayer-swarm), written for playback rather than bulk downloading. It requests the playhead first, then the file's index and a read-ahead window sized from the video's bitrate. When you skip, it cancels requests that are no longer urgent, sends the pieces at the new position to the fastest peers, and duplicates the most urgent blocks to a second peer so one slow peer cannot stall playback.
  • Finds peers fast. HTTP and UDP trackers, the DHT, and peer exchange, with quick first connection attempts and peers that worked before tried first.
  • Paste, drop, or search. Magnet links, .torrent files and links (drag one onto the window), or the built-in search.
  • Instant start for the best result. Each search marks a "Best pick" and quietly preloads its first minutes, so pressing play on it starts at once. One preload at a time, never uploaded, deleted if unused, and off with one switch.
A queue that downloads ahead, intelligently
  • Everything you queue downloads in the background while you watch, so the next video is ready before you get to it. Set a maximum in Settings if you prefer fewer at once.
  • What you are watching always comes first. Every second TorrentPlayer measures your connection and playback's needs. While the buffer is short, the rest of the queue gets only what playback leaves; if playback runs low, the rest pauses briefly to let it catch up, and keeps going if the video's own swarm is the bottleneck. Once you are comfortably ahead, everything runs at full speed again.
  • Live status for every item: download and upload speed, peers, percent downloaded, and time left. Green sections show the downloaded chunks and gaps, matching the player's seek bar; readiness and waiting states are shown separately.
  • Gives back to the swarm. The built-in engine uploads every verified piece it has. Queued torrents keep sharing, finished or not, until you pause or remove them, with one upload limit across both engines.
  • In your order. The queue downloads in the order you set, so series, albums, and courses arrive in sequence; only you reorder it, by dragging or once with Sort by… (name, recently added, size, progress, speed, peers, or time left). Pause any video, a whole torrent, or everything with one click: pausing a torrent or everything stops download and upload until you resume; pausing one video of a torrent stops its download.
  • You stay in charge. Nothing in the queue is paused, removed, or reordered for you, and the next video plays only when you pick it.
A player for video and audio
  • A clean, cinematic player with keyboard controls (Space, ←/→ or the on-screen buttons to skip 10 seconds, F for fullscreen, M to mute, C for captions, Q for the queue), playback speed, and Shift+N to play the next item in the queue. When a video ends, a card offers Play next or Replay; nothing plays on its own.
  • Music, podcasts, and audiobooks (MP3, FLAC, AAC/M4A/M4B, Ogg, Opus, WAV) stream and skip just like video, with a "now playing" view; an album starts at its first track and its tracks queue in order.
  • Subtitles found in the torrent and matched to the video, or loaded from a file.
  • Honest status instead of an endless spinner: download rate, peers, and seconds buffered ahead, plus a debug overlay (D) with a live piece map.
  • Dolby and DTS audio play with sound: AC-3, E-AC-3, TrueHD, and DTS tracks, which the system's web engine cannot decode, are converted to AAC on the fly by a bundled, playback-only FFmpeg; the video itself is untouched.
Find and organize
  • Search public torrent indexers from inside the app. Results stream in as each indexer answers, ranked by relevance and by how watchable they are: seeders, resolution, source quality, HDR, whether the built-in player can play them, and a size check that catches fake 4K. Adult categories are excluded by default.
  • Courses, not file lists. Lectures are natural-sorted ("Lecture 2" before "Lecture 10"), a torrent's videos appear as one course in the queue, and a file explorer previews pictures, text, and subtitles inside a torrent before you play anything.
  • Resume across restarts. Watch progress is saved locally and shown in the queue and Library. Reopening an unfinished video continues from its last position, with a Start over button.
  • Complete files you can find. Finished video and audio downloads are saved with their original names and formats. Copy path appears beside Play when a file is fully saved. The Library's Remove torrent deletes its saved files and cached pieces after confirmation. See Downloads, saved files, and library removal.
Network and privacy controls
  • Three connection modes: direct (with your VPN provider's app connected, OpenVPN-based apps included, traffic goes through it); a built-in WireGuard tunnel that runs inside the app with no administrator rights or separate VPN app; or a SOCKS5 proxy.
  • Kill switch in the WireGuard and SOCKS5 modes. If the tunnel or proxy drops, all traffic stops and open connections close. Nothing falls back to your direct connection, and traffic resumes by itself when the tunnel is back. With your own VPN app, use its kill switch.
  • Incoming peer connections, if you want them (off by default, so there is no firewall prompt): on a chosen or random port, with optional UPnP in Direct mode, or inside the WireGuard tunnel on a port your provider forwards. Never through a SOCKS5 proxy.
  • See your speed and where you appear from. The status bar shows the total download and upload speed of every torrent, and your public IPv4 and IPv6 addresses as the internet sees them, through the current mode (optional; see Privacy).
  • Bandwidth limits for download and upload, applied to the whole app instantly.
  • Sharing you control: pause or remove a torrent to stop sharing it, and a peer cap per torrent.
